newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close up on Dow, re-election hopes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close up on Dow, re-election hopes.

text.p: Brazilian shares closed broadly higher in muscular trade, boosted by strong rises on Wall Street and optimism that Congress' lower house will pass a re-election amendment tonight, brokers said.
"Without a doubt today's rise was due to the expectations on re-election and the Dow Jones' rise," said Roberto Rocha of Banco Tendencia.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares rose 1.17 percent to close at 78,498 points on hefty trade of 618.2 million reais ($591.9 million).
Brokers said trade was up sharply from Monday as investors, egged on buy the strong rise in the Dow, snapped up Brazilian shares, particularly blue chips.

The Dow was behind most of the session's rise, but market watchers are focused on tonights scheduled vote on re-election in Congress' lower house. "Everyone's waiting to see what happens in Brasilia," one dealer said.
The day's rise was led by strong buying in benchmark Telebras. Telebras preferred rose 1.24 percent to close at 90.10 reais while its voting common ended up 1.44 percent at 84.09 reais.
While Telebras shares were not the highest risers, they regularly account for 65 percent of daily trade and set the session's trend.
State mining firm Cia Vale do Rio Doce closed 2.36 percent higher at 23.44 reais while Brazilian state oil monopoly Petrobras ended up 1.06 percent at 190.00 reais.
Among other blue chips, state power holding Eletrobras closed up 2.59 percent to end at 435 reais.
Despite the rise in blue-chip Eletrobras, the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of nine most-liquid shares closed down 0.17 percent to end at 2,289 points.
Among power losers was Minas Gerais state's Cemig, which fell 0.9 percent to end at 43.90 reais.
Some brokers said Brazilian stocks may be hit by profit-taking on Wednesday if re-election passes on its initial vote in the lower house.
But others said today's strong session signals that the market may not be ready for a correction and could continue upward on passage of the government's re-election proposal.
